source_review.notes: Checked all twelve references for identity, edition or revision, publication date, publisher, official status, and domain scope. Official records confirm IEC 61508-2:2010 edition 2 with a 2027 stability date, the ISO 26262:2018 second-edition series, active FAA AC 20-115D and its DO-178C recognition, current FDA recognition of IEC 62304 edition 1.1, ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 edition 2, NASA's maintained software-assurance resources, and ISO 14971:2019 edition 3. Checked publisher, DOI, conference, or author records for Leveson, Knight, Kelly-Weaver, and Bass-Clements-Kazman. Domain standards are not generalized across sectors.

evidence: Defined the nine-field assurance tuple, fault-error-failure chain, claim tuple, channel probability, and common-cause model before use.
Checked set, tuple, exponent, multiplication, subtraction, equality, implication, and configuration notation for consistent scope and GitHub rendering.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Probabilities remain conditional illustrations rather than measured failure rates.

evidence: Recomputed 0.01 squared as 0.0001 and 0.001 plus 0.999 times 0.0001 as 0.0010999.
Recomputed exercise independence as 0.02 squared equals 0.0004 and common-cause estimate as 0.0033988.
Executed safety-command-admission under Python 3.14.4 and observed five exact outputs with empty standard error.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No numerical value is presented as a calibrated safety target or acceptance criterion.

evidence: Verified the common-cause expression reduces to the independent case when q is zero and is dominated by q in the supplied fixture.
Verified process conformance can coexist with an omitted maintenance hazard, refuting conformance-to-safety implication.
Verified two replicas can share a single failure cause, refuting duplication-to-independence implication.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Counterexamples establish insufficiency only; no universal safety theorem is claimed.

evidence: Reviewed startup, normal, degraded, maintenance, partition, overload, failover, restart, update, rollback, recovery, emergency, and retirement states.

Reviewed stale identity, unit error, common power, sensor, processor, compiler, requirement, supplier, security, privacy, accessibility, operator, physical, clinical, rail, warehouse, floodgate, and wildfire cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Qualified domain authorities and affected stakeholders remain necessary for real safety decisions.

evidence: Traced hazard-to-mechanism, configuration-identity, independence, and lifecycle-safety invariants through architecture, assurance, operation, and change.
Confirmed each worked example identifies system consequence, mechanism, evidence boundary, authority, and limitation.
invariant_checking.notes: Conformance, redundancy, testing, proof, or supplier certification never substitutes for the whole assurance argument.

evidence: Reviewed the conformance counterexample for simultaneous process compliance and omitted hazard.
Reviewed the duplication counterexample for simultaneous two-component count and shared failure domain.
Checked the common-cause arithmetic and assumptions separately from safety acceptability.
proof_review.notes: Claims are deliberately limited to non-implication and illustrative sensitivity.

evidence: Audited uses of regulated, safety-critical, criticality, safe, conformance, assurance, independence, diversity, proof, evidence, certification, recognized, current, and qualified.
Confirmed standards applicability, policy, formal evidence, tests, hypothetical examples, local execution, and professional judgment remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter makes no product certification, regulatory approval, or universal safety claim.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet with the repository verifier under CPython 3.14.4 in the recorded local environment.
Confirmed infusion, rail, sensor, medical, warehouse, floodgate, and wildfire cases are hypothetical and not field-tested.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Local execution proves only five finite predicate outputs and no safety threshold, sensor validity, timing guarantee, or real authorization.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed applicability, socio-technical boundaries, hazard-based classification, constraint derivation, interface semantics, authority, degraded modes, containment, common cause, diversity, security interaction, human operation, assurance cases, verification, tools, suppliers, baselines, and change as one coherent advanced architectural treatment.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical failure paths across infusion, rail doors, redundant controllers, sensor substitution, formal models, certificate transition, supplier components, update recovery, warehouse vehicles, floodgates, and wildfire warning. The chapter supplies actionable boundaries, semantics, fault assumptions, evidence, configuration, and lifecycle checks. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate and professional depth, nine-field assurance model, four invariants, one executable predicate, two bounded propositions, one common-cause derivation, eighteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in unfamiliar wildfire transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external regulatory, certification, safety, functional-safety, clinical, medical-device, aviation, automotive, rail, industrial-control, environmental, emergency-management, security, privacy, accessibility, human-factors, supplier, affected-community, academic, or independent practitioner review is claimed. Standards, assurance structures, models, examples, tests, proofs, and local execution do not establish applicability, certification, calibrated failure probability, acceptable residual risk, clinical approval, public authorization, or safe production operation.
